name: Tapo P100 (EU)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only (IEEE 802.11b/g/n). TP-Link lists Bluetooth for setup only.

matter.note: The P100 page lists no Matter support. TP-Link sells a separate Matter-certified model, the Tapo P100M.

apple_home.note: TP-Link lists Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings as the third-party platforms and leaves out Apple Home. There is no HomeKit mode and no Matter. The P100M is the Matter version.

google_home.note: Through the Tapo cloud link (Works with Google Home). Set the plug up in the Tapo app first.

alexa.note: Through the Tapo Alexa skill, linked to your TP-Link account.

smartthings.note: Through the Tapo partner integration in the SmartThings app, signed in with your TP-Link ID.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link Smart Home integration lists the P100 among supported Tapo plugs. Newer devices need your TP-Link account credentials once.

hubRequired.note: Wi-Fi plug that joins your 2.4 GHz router directly and is set up in the Tapo app; no bridge is listed.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link integration controls it over the local network, though newer firmware needs TP-Link account credentials to authenticate. We found no TP-Link page on Tapo-app control without internet.

energyMonitoring.note: TP-Link's plug FAQ says the P110 and P115 measure energy and the P100 does not.

maxLoadWatts.note: 10 A / 2300 W for the EU version, 1/6 HP motor. The UK version is rated 13 A and the US version 10 A / 1200 W; don't mix them up.

summary: The EU Tapo P100 is a basic 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi plug rated 10 A / 2300 W, with no energy monitoring and no Matter. TP-Link lists Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings, all through account linking from the Tapo app. Home Assistant supports it through its TP-Link integration. There is no Apple Home support; the separate Tapo P100M is the Matter version.
caveats: No Apple Home: there is no HomeKit mode and no Matter. Buy the Tapo P100M if you need Apple Home.
Rated 10 A / 2300 W in the EU, lower than the 16 A Tapo P110.
Home Assistant's TP-Link integration asks for your TP-Link account credentials once on newer firmware.
